name: Muscular
summary: Skeletal muscles pull on bones to move the body, hold its posture and steady its joints.

tendon.label: Tendons
tendon.description: Tendons are tough cords and sheets of collagen that tie a muscle to bone. They carry the muscle's pull to the skeleton, so they show where it attaches.

movements.name: Squat
movements.note: Lowering and rising with the feet planted. The hamstrings and trunk muscles steady the hips and spine.

movements.name: Lunge
movements.note: Stepping forward into a split stance and pushing back up; the front leg does most of the work.

movements.name: Deadlift
movements.note: Lifting a weight from the floor by driving the hips forward with a flat back.

movements.name: Glute bridge
movements.note: Lying on the back with knees bent and lifting the hips.

movements.name: Calf raise
movements.note: Rising up onto the balls of the feet.

movements.name: Push-up
movements.note: Lowering the chest to the floor and pressing back up; the trunk is held straight like a plank.

movements.name: Bench press
movements.note: Lying on a bench and pressing a bar up from the chest.

movements.name: Overhead press
movements.note: Pressing a weight from the shoulders to straight overhead.

movements.name: Pull-up
movements.note: Hanging from a bar and pulling the chin up over it.

movements.name: Bent-over row
movements.note: Leaning forward with a flat back and pulling a weight up to the lower ribs.

movements.name: Bicep curl
movements.note: Bending the elbow to lift a weight with the palm facing up.
synergist: humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris
ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris

movements.name: Triceps dip
movements.note: Lowering and pushing the body back up between parallel bars or from a bench.

movements.name: Plank
movements.note: Holding the body straight on the forearms and toes. Nothing moves: the muscles work to hold the position.

movements.name: Crunch
movements.note: Lying on the back and curling the shoulders up toward the hips.

effects.label: Muscle-fiber haze
effects.note: Illustrative effect, not modeled anatomy: glowing streaks that hint at muscle fibers. They run along each part's long axis, not its real fiber directions.

abdominal part of pectoralis major.description: The small lowest part of the chest muscle, arising from the sheath of the abdominal muscles.
abdominal part of pectoralis major.flow: Pulls the raised arm down and across the body

abductor digiti minimi of foot.description: A muscle along the outer edge of the sole, from the heel to the little toe.
abductor digiti minimi of foot.flow: Moves the little toe out and helps support the outer arch

abductor digiti minimi of hand.description: The outermost muscle of the fleshy edge of the palm on the little-finger side (hypothenar eminence).
abductor digiti minimi of hand.flow: Spreads the little finger away from the others

abductor hallucis.description: A muscle along the inner edge of the sole, from the heel to the big toe.
abductor hallucis.flow: Moves the big toe away from the others and supports the arch

abductor pollicis brevis.description: The most superficial muscle of the ball of the thumb (thenar eminence).
abductor pollicis brevis.flow: Moves the thumb away from the palm, at right angles to it

abductor pollicis longus.description: A deep muscle on the back of the forearm whose tendon winds around to the base of the thumb's hand bone.
abductor pollicis longus.flow: Moves the thumb away from the palm and helps tip the wrist toward the thumb

acromial part of deltoid.description: The middle part of the deltoid, running from the acromion at the tip of the shoulder down to the upper arm bone.
acromial part of deltoid.flow: Lifts the arm out to the side

adductor brevis.description: A short adductor lying under pectineus and adductor longus.

adductor longus.description: A fan-shaped muscle at the front of the inner thigh, running from the pubic bone to the middle of the thigh bone.
adductor longus.flow: Draws the thigh inward and helps flex the hip

adductor magnus.description: The largest of the inner-thigh muscles, a big triangle from the pubic and sitting bones to the whole length of the thigh bone.
adductor magnus.flow: Draws the thigh inward; its back part also extends the hip, as in rising from a squat

adductor minimus.description: The upper, separately named part of adductor magnus, running almost horizontally to the thigh bone.
adductor minimus.flow: Draws the thigh inward and turns it outward

anconeus.description: A small triangular muscle on the back of the elbow, running from the outer bump of the arm bone to the ulna.
anconeus.flow: Helps straighten the elbow and steadies it while the forearm turns

aryepiglotticus.description: A thin band continuing on from the oblique arytenoid up to the side of the epiglottis.
aryepiglotticus.flow: Helps pull the epiglottis down and narrow the larynx's entrance when swallowing

ascending part of trapezius.description: The lower fibres of the trapezius, running up from the mid-back vertebrae to the spine of the shoulder blade.
ascending part of trapezius.flow: Pulls the shoulder blade down and helps turn it upward as the arm rises

brachialis.description: A broad muscle under the biceps on the lower half of the arm bone, inserting on the ulna just below the elbow.
brachialis.flow: The elbow's main flexor, whatever the forearm's position

brachioradialis.description: The muscle forming the outer bulge of the forearm below the elbow, running from the lower arm bone to the end of the radius.
brachioradialis.flow: Bends the elbow, most strongly with the thumb pointing up (as in a hammer curl)

buccinator.description: The muscle forming the wall of the cheek, deep to the other facial muscles, running from the jaws to the corner of the mouth.
buccinator.flow: Presses the cheek against the teeth to keep food between them, and helps blow air out

calcaneal tendon.description: The Achilles tendon, the thickest and strongest tendon in the body, joining the calf muscles to the heel bone.
calcaneal tendon.flow: Carries the pull of gastrocnemius and soleus to the heel, pointing the foot down

cervical rotator.description: Small muscles of the neck running from the side process of one vertebra to the spine of the vertebra above, deepest of the back muscles.
cervical rotator.flow: Steady the neck vertebrae and help turn them

clavicular part of deltoid.description: The front part of the deltoid, the rounded cap of the shoulder, running from the outer collarbone to the upper arm bone.
clavicular part of deltoid.flow: Lifts the arm forward and turns it inward

clavicular part of pectoralis major.description: The upper part of the large chest muscle, running from the inner half of the collarbone to the upper arm bone.
clavicular part of pectoralis major.flow: Lifts the arm forward and across the chest, as in an incline press

coccygeus.description: A triangular muscle at the back of the pelvic floor, running from the ischial spine to the edges of the sacrum and coccyx.
coccygeus.flow: Supports the pelvic organs and pulls the coccyx forward

common tendinous ring.description: A ring of tough tissue at the back of the eye socket, around the optic canal, from which the four rectus muscles arise.
common tendinous ring.flow: Anchors the four rectus muscles at the back of the eye socket

coracobrachialis.description: A slender muscle in the upper inner arm, running from the coracoid process of the shoulder blade to the middle of the arm bone.
coracobrachialis.flow: Draws the arm forward and toward the body

corrugator supercilii.description: A small, narrow muscle under the inner end of each eyebrow, beneath frontalis and orbicularis oculi.
corrugator supercilii.flow: Draws the eyebrows down and together, making vertical frown lines

deep part of masseter.description: The smaller inner part of the masseter, running more vertically from the cheekbone arch to the jaw's branch.
deep part of masseter.flow: Closes the jaw and pulls it back slightly

depressor anguli oris.description: A triangular muscle running from the lower edge of the jaw up to the corner of the mouth.
depressor anguli oris.flow: Pulls the corner of the mouth down, as in a frown

depressor labii inferioris.description: A square-shaped muscle running from the jaw up into the lower lip, partly under depressor anguli oris.
depressor labii inferioris.flow: Pulls the lower lip down and out, as in a pout of disgust

depressor septi nasi.description: A tiny muscle under the nose that runs from above the upper front teeth to the base of the nasal septum.
depressor septi nasi.flow: Pulls the tip of the nose down and helps widen the nostrils

descending part of trapezius.description: The upper fibres of the trapezius, the large diamond-shaped muscle of the upper back, running from the skull and neck down to the collarbone.
descending part of trapezius.flow: Lifts the shoulder blade (shrugging) and turns it so the arm can rise overhead

diaphragm.description: The dome-shaped sheet of muscle that separates the chest from the abdomen, attached all around the lower rib cage and the lumbar spine.
diaphragm.flow: The main muscle of breathing: it flattens as it contracts, drawing air into the lungs

digastric.description: A muscle with two bellies joined by a round tendon that slings through a loop on the hyoid bone, under the jaw.
digastric.flow: Opens the mouth and raises the hyoid bone when swallowing

extensor carpi radialis brevis.description: A muscle alongside extensor carpi radialis longus, starting at the outer elbow; its tendon is the one most involved in "tennis elbow".
extensor carpi radialis brevis.flow: Straightens (lifts) the wrist and steadies it while gripping

extensor carpi radialis longus.description: A muscle on the thumb side of the forearm's back, starting just above the outer elbow and ending at the base of the index finger's hand bone.
extensor carpi radialis longus.flow: Straightens (lifts) the wrist and tips the hand toward the thumb

extensor carpi ulnaris.description: A long muscle on the little-finger side of the back of the forearm, ending at the base of the fifth hand bone.
extensor carpi ulnaris.flow: Straightens the wrist and tips the hand toward the little finger

extensor digiti minimi.description: A slim muscle beside extensor digitorum that sends a tendon to the little finger.

extensor digitorum.description: The main finger-straightening muscle on the back of the forearm, splitting into four tendons across the back of the hand.
extensor digitorum.flow: Straightens the fingers and helps lift the wrist

extensor digitorum brevis.description: A small, fleshy muscle on the top of the foot that sends tendons to the second to fourth toes.

extensor digitorum longus.description: A muscle on the front outer shin whose tendon splits into four across the top of the foot to the small toes.
extensor digitorum longus.flow: Lifts the four small toes and the foot

extensor hallucis brevis.description: The innermost slip of the short toe-extensor on the top of the foot, running to the big toe.

extensor hallucis longus.description: A thin muscle between tibialis anterior and extensor digitorum longus, whose tendon runs to the big toe.
extensor hallucis longus.flow: Lifts the big toe and helps lift the foot

extensor indicis.description: A narrow, deep muscle on the lower back of the ulna that sends a tendon to the index finger.
extensor indicis.flow: Straightens the index finger on its own, as in pointing

extensor pollicis brevis.description: A deep forearm muscle whose tendon runs beside that of abductor pollicis longus to the thumb's first joint.
extensor pollicis brevis.flow: Straightens the thumb at its knuckle

extensor pollicis longus.description: A deep forearm muscle whose tendon hooks around a bony bump on the radius on its way to the thumb tip.
extensor pollicis longus.flow: Straightens the thumb at all its joints and pulls it back

external anal sphincter.description: A ring of voluntary muscle around the anal canal.
external anal sphincter.flow: Keeps the anus closed and can be tightened at will

external intercostal muscle.description: The outer layer of muscle in each gap between the ribs, its fibres slanting down and forward.
external intercostal muscle.flow: Lifts the ribs to help breathe in

external oblique.description: The largest and outermost of the three flat abdominal muscles, its fibres running down and forward from the lower ribs.
external oblique.flow: Bends and twists the trunk (to the opposite side) and squeezes the belly

fibularis brevis.description: A muscle under fibularis longus on the outside of the leg, ending on the outer edge of the foot.
fibularis brevis.flow: Turns the sole of the foot outward and helps point it down

fibularis longus.description: A long muscle on the outside of the leg whose tendon runs behind the outer ankle and right across the sole.
fibularis longus.flow: Points the foot down, turns its sole outward and supports the arches

fibularis tertius.description: A small, often variable part split off the lower extensor digitorum longus, ending on the fifth foot bone.
fibularis tertius.flow: Lifts the foot and turns its sole outward

first lumbrical of foot.description: A small, worm-shaped muscle in the sole, starting on a tendon of flexor digitorum longus and running to the second toe.
first lumbrical of foot.flow: Bends the second toe at its base and straightens its other joints

first plantar interosseous of foot.description: A small muscle on the sole side between the foot bones, running to the third toe.
first plantar interosseous of foot.flow: Draws the third toe toward the second

flexor accessorius.description: A flat, square muscle (quadratus plantae) in the sole that joins the tendon of flexor digitorum longus.
flexor accessorius.flow: Straightens the pull of flexor digitorum longus so the toes curl straight

flexor carpi radialis.description: A superficial forearm muscle running from the inner elbow to the base of the second and third hand bones on the thumb side.
flexor carpi radialis.flow: Bends the wrist and tips the hand toward the thumb

flexor digiti minimi brevis of foot.description: A small muscle in the outer sole, under the fifth foot bone.
flexor digiti minimi brevis of foot.flow: Bends the little toe at its base

flexor digiti minimi brevis of hand.description: A small muscle of the little-finger side of the palm, beside abductor digiti minimi.
flexor digiti minimi brevis of hand.flow: Bends the little finger at its knuckle

flexor digitorum brevis.description: The central muscle of the sole's first layer, running from the heel to the four small toes.

flexor digitorum longus.description: A deep muscle on the back of the shin whose tendon passes behind the inner ankle and splits into four for the toes.
flexor digitorum longus.flow: Curls the four small toes and helps point the foot

flexor digitorum profundus.description: A deep forearm muscle on the ulna, with four tendons that pass through splits in the superficialis tendons to the fingertips.
flexor digitorum profundus.flow: Bends the fingertips, and with them the whole finger, as in gripping

flexor digitorum superficialis.description: A large forearm muscle under the superficial layer, with four tendons running through the wrist to the middle bones of the fingers.
flexor digitorum superficialis.flow: Bends the fingers at their middle joints, and helps bend the wrist

flexor hallucis longus.description: A deep, powerful muscle on the back of the fibula whose tendon runs under the foot to the tip of the big toe.
flexor hallucis longus.flow: Bends the big toe and helps push off when walking

flexor pollicis brevis.description: A short muscle in the ball of the thumb, beside abductor pollicis brevis and over opponens pollicis.
flexor pollicis brevis.flow: Bends the thumb at its knuckle

flexor pollicis longus.description: A deep forearm muscle on the radius whose tendon runs through the wrist to the tip of the thumb.
flexor pollicis longus.flow: Bends the tip of the thumb

fourth lumbrical of foot.description: A small, worm-shaped muscle in the sole that runs from the long flexor tendons to the little toe.
fourth lumbrical of foot.flow: Bends the little toe at its base and straightens its other joints

frontalis.description: The front belly of the scalp muscle, a thin sheet over the forehead. It has no bony insertion; it pulls on the skin of the brows.
frontalis.flow: Raises the eyebrows and wrinkles the forehead

gemellus inferior.description: A small muscle running from the sitting bone (ischial tuberosity) to the tendon of obturator internus.

gemellus superior.description: A small muscle running from the ischial spine to the tendon of obturator internus.

genioglossus.description: The fan-shaped muscle making up most of the tongue's bulk, running from the inside of the chin into the whole length of the tongue.
genioglossus.flow: Pushes the tongue forward and out and draws its middle down

geniohyoid.description: A narrow muscle just above the mylohyoid, running from the inside of the chin back to the hyoid bone.
geniohyoid.flow: Pulls the hyoid bone forward and up, widening the throat, and helps open the mouth

gluteus maximus.description: The large, thick muscle of the buttock, running from the back of the pelvis and sacrum to the thigh bone and the iliotibial tract.
gluteus maximus.flow: Extends the hip powerfully (rising from a squat, climbing, sprinting) and turns the thigh outward

gluteus medius.description: A thick, fan-shaped muscle on the outer hip, partly under gluteus maximus, ending on the top of the thigh bone (greater trochanter).
gluteus medius.flow: Moves the thigh out to the side and keeps the pelvis level when you stand on one leg

gluteus minimus.description: The smallest and deepest of the gluteal muscles, under gluteus medius.
gluteus minimus.flow: Moves the thigh out to the side, turns it inward and keeps the pelvis level when walking

gracilis.description: A long, thin strap muscle on the inner thigh, running from the pubic bone to the inside of the shin below the knee.
gracilis.flow: Draws the thigh inward and helps bend the knee

humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris.description: The head of flexor carpi ulnaris that starts at the inner elbow; the muscle ends on the pisiform bone at the little-finger side of the wrist.
humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris.flow: Bends the wrist and tips the hand toward the little finger

humeral head of pronator teres.description: The larger head of pronator teres, starting from the inner bump of the arm bone (medial epicondyle) and slanting across to the radius.
humeral head of pronator teres.flow: Turns the palm down and helps bend the elbow

hyoglossus.description: A thin, flat muscle running up from the hyoid bone into the side of the tongue.
hyoglossus.flow: Pulls the sides of the tongue down and back

iliacus.description: A fan-shaped muscle filling the inner bowl of the hip bone; its tendon joins that of psoas major.
iliacus.flow: Flexes the hip together with psoas major

iliococcygeus.description: The thin back part of the levator ani, running from a band on the pelvic side wall to the coccyx.
iliococcygeus.flow: Supports the pelvic organs and raises the pelvic floor

iliocostalis cervicis.description: The neck part of iliocostalis, the outermost column of the erector spinae, running from the upper ribs to the neck vertebrae.
iliocostalis cervicis.flow: Extends the neck and bends it to its own side

iliocostalis lumborum.description: The lower-back part of iliocostalis, the outermost column of the erector spinae, running from the pelvis to the lower ribs.
iliocostalis lumborum.flow: Straightens and holds up the lower spine and bends it to its own side

iliocostalis thoracis.description: The chest part of iliocostalis, the outermost column of the erector spinae, linking the lower ribs to the upper ribs.
iliocostalis thoracis.flow: Straightens the spine and bends it to its own side

inferior head of lateral pterygoid.description: The larger, lower head of the lateral pterygoid, running back from the skull base to the neck of the jaw.
inferior head of lateral pterygoid.flow: Pulls the jaw forward and opens the mouth; one side alone swings the jaw to the other side

inferior oblique.description: The only eye-moving muscle that starts at the front of the eye socket, curving under the eyeball to its outer back side.
inferior oblique.flow: Turns the eye upward and outward and rotates its top outward

inferior oblique part of longus colli.description: The lower slanting part of longus colli, running from the upper chest vertebrae to the lower neck vertebrae.
inferior oblique part of longus colli.flow: Bends the neck forward and helps turn it to the opposite side

inferior pharyngeal constrictor.description: The thickest and lowest of the three throat-wrapping muscles, arising from the cartilages of the larynx.
inferior pharyngeal constrictor.flow: Squeezes the lower throat to push food into the oesophagus; its lowest fibres act as the upper oesophageal sphincter

inferior rectus.description: One of the six muscles that move the eyeball, running from the back of the eye socket to the underside of the eye.
inferior rectus.flow: Turns the eye downward (and slightly inward)

infraspinatus.description: A thick rotator cuff muscle covering most of the back of the shoulder blade below its spine.
infraspinatus.flow: Turns the arm outward and holds the head of the arm bone in its socket

innermost intercostal muscle.description: The deepest layer of muscle between the ribs, separated from the internal intercostals by the intercostal nerves and vessels.
innermost intercostal muscle.flow: Helps the internal intercostals move the ribs when breathing

internal intercostal muscle.description: The middle layer of muscle between the ribs, its fibres slanting down and back, across the external intercostals.
internal intercostal muscle.flow: Pulls the ribs down to help breathe out forcefully

internal oblique.description: The middle of the three flat abdominal muscles, its fibres running up and forward, across those of the external oblique.
internal oblique.flow: Bends and twists the trunk (to its own side) and squeezes the belly

interspinalis thoracis.description: Short muscles between the spines of neighbouring chest vertebrae, mostly at the top and bottom of the chest spine.
interspinalis thoracis.flow: Help extend and steady the spine

lateral crico-arytenoid.description: A small muscle on the side of the voice box, running from the cricoid cartilage up to an arytenoid cartilage.
lateral crico-arytenoid.flow: Swings the vocal cords together to close the gap between them for speaking

lateral head of flexor hallucis brevis.description: The outer head of the short flexor of the big toe, deep in the sole; its tendon holds the outer sesamoid bone.
lateral head of flexor hallucis brevis.flow: Bends the big toe at its base

lateral head of gastrocnemius.description: The outer head of the calf muscle, starting on the thigh bone above the knee and ending in the Achilles tendon.
lateral head of gastrocnemius.flow: Points the foot down (rising onto the toes) and helps bend the knee

lateral head of triceps brachii.description: The outer head of the triceps, starting high on the back of the arm bone, forming the horseshoe shape of a toned arm.

lateral lumbar intertransversarius.description: Small muscles bridging the side processes of neighbouring lower-back vertebrae.
lateral lumbar intertransversarius.flow: Bend the lower spine to their own side

lateral rectus.description: An eye-moving muscle running along the outer wall of the eye socket to the outer side of the eye.
lateral rectus.flow: Turns the eye outward, away from the nose

latissimus dorsi.description: The broadest muscle of the back, sweeping from the lower spine and pelvis up to the front of the upper arm bone.
latissimus dorsi.flow: Pulls the arm down and back and turns it inward, as in a pull-up or rowing

levator anguli oris.description: A muscle running from the upper jaw, beneath levator labii superioris, down to the corner of the mouth.
levator anguli oris.flow: Lifts the corner of the mouth, helping to deepen the smile line

levator labii superioris.description: A flat muscle running from just below the eye socket down into the upper lip.
levator labii superioris.flow: Raises and turns out the upper lip

levator labii superioris alaeque nasi.description: A thin strip running down the side of the nose from the upper jaw to the nostril and upper lip.
levator labii superioris alaeque nasi.flow: Lifts the upper lip and flares the nostril, as in a snarl

levator palpebrae superioris.description: A thin muscle inside the eye socket, above the eyeball, that fans out into the upper eyelid.

levator scapulae.description: A strap muscle running from the upper four neck vertebrae down to the top inner corner of the shoulder blade.
levator scapulae.flow: Lifts the shoulder blade and turns it to tip the shoulder down; also bends the neck to its own side

levator veli palatini.description: A muscle running from the skull base near the ear tube down into the soft palate.
levator veli palatini.flow: Lifts the soft palate to seal off the nose when swallowing, and helps open the ear tube

long head of biceps brachii.description: The outer head of the biceps; its long tendon starts just above the shoulder socket and runs over the head of the arm bone.
long head of biceps brachii.flow: Bends the elbow, turns the palm up and helps lift the arm forward

long head of biceps femoris.description: The outer hamstring's long head, running from the sitting bone to the head of the fibula below the outer knee.
long head of biceps femoris.flow: Bends the knee and extends the hip

long head of triceps brachii.description: The inner head of the triceps on the back of the arm, the only one starting on the shoulder blade (just below the socket).
long head of triceps brachii.flow: Straightens the elbow and helps pull the arm back and down

longissimus capitis.description: The top of the longissimus column, running from the lower neck and upper chest vertebrae to the bony bump behind the ear.
longissimus capitis.flow: Extends the head and turns it to its own side

longissimus cervicis.description: The neck part of longissimus, running from the upper chest vertebrae to the neck vertebrae.
longissimus cervicis.flow: Extends the neck and bends it to its own side

longissimus thoracis.description: The largest part of the erector spinae, a long column running from the pelvis and lower back up to the ribs and chest vertebrae.
longissimus thoracis.flow: Straightens the spine and holds it upright, and bends it to its own side

longus capitis.description: A deep muscle on the front of the upper neck vertebrae that reaches up to the base of the skull.
longus capitis.flow: Bends the head and upper neck forward

lumbar rotator.description: Small, deep muscles in the lower back running from one vertebra to the one above.
lumbar rotator.flow: Steady the lower-back vertebrae and sense their position

medial head of flexor hallucis brevis.description: The inner head of the short flexor of the big toe, deep in the sole; its tendon holds the inner sesamoid bone.
medial head of flexor hallucis brevis.flow: Bends the big toe at its base

medial head of gastrocnemius.description: The larger, inner head of the calf muscle, starting above the knee on the thigh bone and ending in the Achilles tendon.
medial head of gastrocnemius.flow: Points the foot down (rising onto the toes) and helps bend the knee

medial head of triceps brachii.description: The deepest head of the triceps, lying under the other two along the lower back of the arm bone.
medial head of triceps brachii.flow: Straightens the elbow, working in every elbow extension

medial lumbar intertransversarius.description: Small muscles linking the small bony bumps on the backs of neighbouring lower-back vertebrae.
medial lumbar intertransversarius.flow: Steady the lower-back vertebrae and bend the spine to the side

medial pterygoid.description: A thick, square muscle on the inner side of the jaw's branch, mirroring the masseter on the outside.
medial pterygoid.flow: Closes the jaw and moves it forward and to the opposite side when grinding food

medial rectus.description: The largest of the eye-moving muscles, running along the inner (nose-side) wall of the eye socket.
medial rectus.flow: Turns the eye inward, toward the nose

mentalis.description: A small cone of muscle on the chin, running from the jaw just below the lower front teeth into the chin's skin.
mentalis.flow: Raises and wrinkles the chin skin and pushes the lower lip out, as in pouting

middle pharyngeal constrictor.description: The middle of the three throat-wrapping muscles, fanning out from the hyoid bone.
middle pharyngeal constrictor.flow: Squeezes the middle of the throat to push food down when swallowing

multifidus cervicis.description: The neck part of multifidus, short bundles crossing two to four vertebrae, deep against the spine.
multifidus cervicis.flow: Steadies the neck vertebrae, extends the neck and helps turn it

multifidus lumborum.description: The thickest part of multifidus, filling the groove beside the lower-back spine down to the sacrum.
multifidus lumborum.flow: Holds the lower-back vertebrae steady and extends the lower spine

multifidus thoracis.description: The chest part of multifidus, short bundles crossing two to four vertebrae, deep against the spine.
multifidus thoracis.flow: Steadies the spine, extends it and helps turn it

mylohyoid.description: A flat sheet that runs between the two sides of the lower jaw, forming the muscular floor of the mouth.
mylohyoid.flow: Raises the floor of the mouth and the tongue when swallowing, and helps open the mouth

nasalis.description: A small muscle over the side of the nose, with a part that crosses the bridge and a part at the nostril.
nasalis.flow: Compresses the bridge of the nose and flares or narrows the nostrils

oblique arytenoid.description: Two crossing slips of muscle on the back of the arytenoid cartilages, forming an X.
oblique arytenoid.flow: Draws the arytenoid cartilages together to help close the larynx

oblique head of adductor hallucis.description: The larger head of adductor hallucis, running obliquely across the deep sole to the big toe.
oblique head of adductor hallucis.flow: Draws the big toe toward the others and supports the arch

oblique head of adductor pollicis.description: The upper head of adductor pollicis, deep in the palm, starting from the wrist bones and the bases of the middle hand bones.
oblique head of adductor pollicis.flow: Pulls the thumb toward the palm, as in a key grip

oblique part of cricothyroid.description: The more slanted part of the cricothyroid, on the outside front of the voice box.
oblique part of cricothyroid.flow: Slides the thyroid cartilage forward to tighten the vocal cords, raising pitch

obliquus capitis inferior.description: A suboccipital muscle running from the spine of the axis to the side of the atlas; it is the only one that does not reach the skull.
obliquus capitis inferior.flow: Turns the atlas, and with it the head, to its own side

obliquus capitis superior.description: A short suboccipital muscle running from the side of the atlas up and back to the skull.
obliquus capitis superior.flow: Tips the head back and tilts it to its own side

obturator externus.description: A fan-shaped muscle covering the outer face of the large opening in the hip bone (obturator foramen), passing under the hip joint.
obturator externus.flow: Turns the thigh outward and steadies the hip

obturator internus.description: A fan-shaped muscle inside the pelvis whose tendon turns sharply around the hip bone to reach the thigh bone.
obturator internus.flow: Turns the thigh outward and steadies the head of the thigh bone in its socket

occipitalis.description: The back belly of the scalp muscle, over the back of the skull. It anchors the tough sheet (galea aponeurotica) that links it to frontalis.

omohyoid.description: A long, thin muscle with two bellies linked by a tendon, running from the top of the shoulder blade to the hyoid bone.
omohyoid.flow: Pulls the hyoid bone down and steadies it

opponens digiti minimi of foot.description: A small, often absent slip deep in the outer sole, running to the fifth foot bone.
opponens digiti minimi of foot.flow: Draws the fifth foot bone down and in

opponens digiti minimi of hand.description: A muscle under the other little-finger muscles of the palm, attached along the fifth hand bone.
opponens digiti minimi of hand.flow: Cups the palm by drawing the little finger's hand bone forward to meet the thumb

opponens pollicis.description: A muscle under the other two of the ball of the thumb, attached along the whole thumb hand bone.
opponens pollicis.flow: Swings the thumb across the palm to meet the fingertips (opposition)

orbicularis oris.description: The ring of muscle inside the lips, formed largely from fibres of the other muscles that meet at the mouth.
orbicularis oris.flow: Closes and purses the lips, as in whistling, kissing and speaking

orbital part of orbicularis oculi.description: The outer ring of the muscle that encircles the eye, spreading over the bony rim of the eye socket.
orbital part of orbicularis oculi.flow: Shuts the eyelids tightly, as when squinting or squeezing the eyes shut

palatopharyngeus.description: A thin muscle running from the soft palate down the inside of the throat, forming the back arch of the tonsil.
palatopharyngeus.flow: Lifts the throat and larynx and narrows the passage to the nose when swallowing

palmaris longus.description: A small muscle with a long, thin tendon that runs into the palm; about one person in seven lacks it on one side or both.
palmaris longus.flow: Tenses the palm's fibrous sheet and helps bend the wrist

palpebral part of orbicularis oculi.description: The thin inner part of the eye's ring muscle, lying within the eyelids themselves.
palpebral part of orbicularis oculi.flow: Closes the eyelids gently, as in blinking and sleep

pectineus.description: A flat, square muscle at the top of the inner thigh, between the pubic bone and the upper thigh bone.
pectineus.flow: Draws the thigh inward and flexes the hip

pectoralis minor.description: A thin, triangular muscle under pectoralis major, running from the third to fifth ribs up to the coracoid process of the shoulder blade.
pectoralis minor.flow: Pulls the shoulder blade forward and down, and lifts the ribs when breathing hard

piriformis.description: A pear-shaped muscle running from the front of the sacrum out through the greater sciatic notch to the top of the thigh bone; the sciatic nerve passes just below it.
piriformis.flow: Turns the thigh outward, or moves it out to the side when the hip is bent

plantaris.description: A small muscle with a very long, thin tendon, lying between gastrocnemius and soleus; it is absent in some people.
plantaris.flow: Weakly helps point the foot and bend the knee

platysma.description: A broad, very thin sheet of muscle just under the skin of the front of the neck, running from the upper chest up over the jaw.
platysma.flow: Tenses the skin of the neck and pulls the corners of the mouth down

popliteus.description: A thin, triangular muscle behind the knee, from the outer thigh bone to the back of the shin.
popliteus.flow: Unlocks the straightened knee by turning the shin inward, so it can start to bend

posterior crico-arytenoid.description: A muscle on the back of the voice box, running from the cricoid cartilage to the arytenoid cartilages.
posterior crico-arytenoid.flow: The only muscle that opens the vocal cords, keeping the airway open for breathing

procerus.description: A small muscle over the bridge of the nose that blends into the forehead skin between the eyebrows.
procerus.flow: Pulls the inner eyebrows down, making horizontal wrinkles across the nose bridge (as in a frown)

pronator quadratus.description: A flat, square muscle across the lower front of the forearm, deep against the radius and ulna.
pronator quadratus.flow: The main muscle that turns the palm down

psoas major.description: A long, thick muscle running from the sides of the lower spine through the pelvis to the inner thigh bone, joining iliacus as the iliopsoas.
psoas major.flow: The strongest hip flexor: lifts the thigh, or bends the trunk forward when the legs are fixed

pubococcygeus.description: Part of the levator ani, the pelvic floor's main muscle, running from the back of the pubic bone to the coccyx.
pubococcygeus.flow: Supports the pelvic organs and helps control urination

puborectalis.description: Part of the levator ani that loops like a sling around the back of the rectum from the pubic bone.
puborectalis.flow: Pulls the end of the rectum forward to keep stool in

pyramidalis.description: A small triangular muscle in front of the bottom of rectus abdominis, just above the pubic bone; some people lack it.
pyramidalis.flow: Tenses the midline seam of the belly wall (linea alba)

quadratus femoris.description: A flat, square muscle running from the sitting bone across to the back of the thigh bone.

quadratus lumborum.description: A thick, square muscle deep in the lower back, between the lowest rib, the lower-back vertebrae and the top of the pelvis.
quadratus lumborum.flow: Bends the lower spine to its own side, hitches up the hip, and steadies the lowest rib when breathing in

rectus abdominis.description: The long, strap-like muscle down the front of the belly, from the lower ribs to the pubic bone, crossed by tendinous bands that form the "six-pack".
rectus abdominis.flow: Bends the trunk forward, as in a crunch, and steadies the pelvis

rectus capitis anterior.description: A short muscle running from the front of the first neck vertebra (atlas) to the base of the skull.
rectus capitis anterior.flow: Nods the head forward and steadies the joint between skull and atlas

rectus capitis lateralis.description: A short muscle running from the side of the first neck vertebra (atlas) up to the skull base.
rectus capitis lateralis.flow: Tilts the head to its own side

rectus capitis posterior major.description: One of the small suboccipital muscles under the back of the skull, running from the second neck vertebra (axis) to the skull.
rectus capitis posterior major.flow: Tips the head back and turns it to its own side

rectus capitis posterior minor.description: The smallest suboccipital muscle, running from the back of the first neck vertebra (atlas) to the skull.

rectus femoris.description: The middle quadriceps muscle at the front of the thigh, the only one that crosses the hip as well as the knee.
rectus femoris.flow: Straightens the knee and helps flex the hip, as in kicking

rhomboid major.description: A flat, four-sided muscle under the trapezius, running from the upper chest vertebrae to the inner edge of the shoulder blade.
rhomboid major.flow: Pulls the shoulder blade back toward the spine and up

rhomboid minor.description: A small strip just above rhomboid major, running from the lowest neck vertebrae to the shoulder blade.
rhomboid minor.flow: Pulls the shoulder blade back toward the spine

risorius.description: A thin, variable band that runs across the cheek to the corner of the mouth from the fascia over the parotid gland.
risorius.flow: Pulls the corner of the mouth sideways, as in a grimace

salpingopharyngeus.description: A slender muscle running from the opening of the ear tube down the side wall of the throat.
salpingopharyngeus.flow: Lifts the throat when swallowing and helps open the ear tube

sartorius.description: The longest muscle in the body, a strap running diagonally across the front of the thigh from the front of the hip bone to the inside of the knee.
sartorius.flow: Flexes, spreads and turns out the hip and bends the knee, as when sitting cross-legged

scalenus anterior.description: A muscle on the side of the neck running from the neck vertebrae down to the first rib, with the main nerves to the arm passing behind it.
scalenus anterior.flow: Raises the first rib when breathing hard and bends the neck to its own side

scalenus medius.description: The longest of the scalene muscles, running from most of the neck vertebrae down to the first rib.
scalenus medius.flow: Raises the first rib when breathing hard and bends the neck to its own side

scalenus posterior.description: The smallest and deepest-lying scalene muscle, running from the lower neck vertebrae to the second rib.
scalenus posterior.flow: Raises the second rib when breathing hard and bends the neck to its own side

second lumbrical of foot.description: A small, worm-shaped muscle in the sole that runs from the long flexor tendons to the third toe.
second lumbrical of foot.flow: Bends the third toe at its base and straightens its other joints

second plantar interosseous of foot.description: A small muscle on the sole side between the foot bones, running to the fourth toe.
second plantar interosseous of foot.flow: Draws the fourth toe toward the second

semimembranosus.description: The broad inner hamstring muscle under semitendinosus, named for its flat, membrane-like upper tendon.
semimembranosus.flow: Bends the knee and extends the hip, and turns the leg inward when the knee is bent

semispinalis capitis.description: A broad, thick muscle on the back of the neck, under splenius, running from the upper spine to the back of the skull.
semispinalis capitis.flow: Extends the head and turns it slightly to the opposite side

semispinalis cervicis.description: A deep back muscle running from the side processes of the chest vertebrae up to the spines of the neck vertebrae.
semispinalis cervicis.flow: Extends the neck and turns it to the opposite side

semispinalis thoracis.description: A deep back muscle crossing several vertebrae, from the side processes of lower chest vertebrae to the spines of higher ones.
semispinalis thoracis.flow: Extends the upper spine and turns it to the opposite side

semitendinosus.description: An inner hamstring muscle named for its long, cord-like lower tendon, which ends on the inner shin.
semitendinosus.flow: Bends the knee and extends the hip, and turns the leg inward when the knee is bent

serratus anterior.description: A muscle with saw-toothed slips on the side of the chest, running from the upper eight or nine ribs around to the inner edge of the shoulder blade.
serratus anterior.flow: Pulls the shoulder blade forward around the chest, as in punching or pushing, and turns it upward

serratus posterior inferior.description: A thin muscle in the lower back, running from the spine up and out to the lowest four ribs.
serratus posterior inferior.flow: Pulls the lowest ribs down and back

serratus posterior superior.description: A thin muscle under the rhomboids, running from the lower neck and upper chest spine down to the upper ribs.
serratus posterior superior.flow: Raises the upper ribs, which may help breathing in

set of anterior cervical intertransversa.description: Tiny muscles bridging the front parts of the side processes of neighbouring neck vertebrae.
set of anterior cervical intertransversa.flow: Bend the neck to their own side and steady the vertebrae

set of dorsal interossei of foot.description: Four two-headed muscles filling the spaces between the foot bones.
set of dorsal interossei of foot.flow: Spread the toes apart from the second toe

set of dorsal interossei of hand.description: Four two-headed muscles filling the gaps between the hand bones, felt on the back of the hand.
set of dorsal interossei of hand.flow: Spread the fingers apart from the middle finger

set of interspinales cervicis.description: Short muscles running between the spines of neighbouring neck vertebrae, either side of the midline.
set of interspinales cervicis.flow: Extend the neck and steady its vertebrae

set of interspinales lumborum.description: Short muscles bridging the spines of neighbouring lower-back vertebrae, either side of the midline.
set of interspinales lumborum.flow: Help extend and steady the lower spine

set of levatores costarum breves.description: Small muscles running from the side process of a vertebra to the rib just below.
set of levatores costarum breves.flow: Raise the ribs and help bend and turn the spine

set of levatores costarum longi.description: Small muscles that run from the side process of a vertebra, skipping a rib, to the rib two below.
set of levatores costarum longi.flow: Raise the ribs and help bend and turn the spine

set of lumbricals of hand.description: Four small, worm-shaped muscles in the palm that start on the tendons of flexor digitorum profundus.
set of lumbricals of hand.flow: Bend the fingers at the knuckles while straightening their middle and end joints

set of palmar interossei of hand.description: Small muscles between the hand bones on the palm side.
set of palmar interossei of hand.flow: Draw the fingers together toward the middle finger

set of posterior cervical intertransvers.description: Tiny muscles bridging the back parts of the side processes of neighbouring neck vertebrae.
set of posterior cervical intertransvers.flow: Bend the neck to their own side and steady the vertebrae

short head of biceps brachii.description: The inner head of the biceps, starting from the coracoid process of the shoulder blade; it joins the long head to insert on the radius.
short head of biceps brachii.flow: Bends the elbow, turns the palm up and helps lift the arm forward

short head of biceps femoris.description: The outer hamstring's short head, starting on the back of the thigh bone; it crosses only the knee.
short head of biceps femoris.flow: Bends the knee and turns the leg outward when the knee is bent

soleus.description: A broad, flat muscle under the gastrocnemius that joins it in the Achilles tendon.
soleus.flow: Points the foot down and keeps the body from tipping forward when standing

spinal part of deltoid.description: The back part of the deltoid, running from the spine of the shoulder blade to the upper arm bone.
spinal part of deltoid.flow: Draws the arm backward and turns it outward

spinalis cervicis.description: The neck part of spinalis, the innermost column of the erector spinae, running between the spines of the neck vertebrae.

spinalis thoracis.description: The innermost column of the erector spinae, running from spine to spine along the chest vertebrae.

splenius capitis.description: A broad, flat muscle on the back of the neck, running from the spine up and out to the base of the skull behind the ear.
splenius capitis.flow: Extends the head and neck and turns the head to its own side

splenius cervicis.description: A flat muscle running from the upper chest vertebrae up to the upper neck vertebrae, below splenius capitis.
splenius cervicis.flow: Extends the neck and turns it to its own side

sternocleidomastoid.description: The prominent strap running diagonally up the side of the neck, from the breastbone and collarbone to the bony bump behind the ear.
sternocleidomastoid.flow: One side turns the head to the opposite side and tilts it toward its own shoulder; both together bend the neck forward

sternocostal part of pectoralis major.description: The large middle part of the chest muscle, running from the breastbone and upper rib cartilages to the upper arm bone.
sternocostal part of pectoralis major.flow: Pulls the arm across the body and turns it inward, as in a push-up or bench press

sternohyoid.description: A thin strap muscle running up the front of the neck from the breastbone to the hyoid bone.
sternohyoid.flow: Pulls the hyoid bone down after swallowing

sternothyroid.description: A strap muscle beneath the sternohyoid, running from the breastbone up to the thyroid cartilage of the voice box.
sternothyroid.flow: Pulls the voice box down after swallowing

straight part of cricothyroid.description: The more vertical part of the cricothyroid, the only voice-box muscle on the outside of the larynx.
straight part of cricothyroid.flow: Tilts the thyroid cartilage forward to stretch the vocal cords, raising the voice's pitch

stylohyoid.description: A slender muscle running from the styloid process under the ear down to the hyoid bone, split by the digastric's tendon.
stylohyoid.flow: Pulls the hyoid bone up and back when swallowing

stylopharyngeus.description: A long, thin muscle running from a spike of bone under the ear (the styloid process) down into the throat wall.
stylopharyngeus.flow: Lifts and widens the throat when swallowing and speaking

subclavius.description: A small, rounded muscle under the collarbone, running from the first rib to the collarbone.
subclavius.flow: Pulls the collarbone down and steadies it during shoulder movements

subscapularis.description: The largest rotator cuff muscle, filling the front surface of the shoulder blade, against the ribs.
subscapularis.flow: Turns the arm inward and holds the head of the arm bone in its socket

superficial head of flexor pollicis brev.description: The main head of flexor pollicis brevis, in the ball of the thumb beside abductor pollicis brevis.
superficial head of flexor pollicis brev.flow: Bends the thumb at its knuckle

superficial part of masseter.description: The larger, outer part of the masseter, the thick muscle over the angle of the jaw that you feel bulge when you clench.
superficial part of masseter.flow: Closes the jaw powerfully and pulls it forward slightly

superior head of lateral pterygoid.description: The upper head of the lateral pterygoid, running nearly horizontally from the skull base to the jaw joint's capsule and disc.
superior head of lateral pterygoid.flow: Steadies the jaw joint's disc as the jaw closes

superior oblique.description: A long, thin eye muscle whose tendon loops through a small fibrous pulley (the trochlea) before reaching the top of the eye.
superior oblique.flow: Turns the eye downward and outward and rotates its top inward

superior oblique part of longus colli.description: The upper slanting part of longus colli, the deep muscle on the front of the neck vertebrae, rising to the first vertebra (atlas).
superior oblique part of longus colli.flow: Bends the neck forward and helps turn it

superior pharyngeal constrictor.description: The uppermost of three curved muscles that wrap the back and sides of the throat, behind the nose and mouth.
superior pharyngeal constrictor.flow: Squeezes the upper throat in sequence to push food down when swallowing

superior rectus.description: One of the six muscles that move the eyeball, running from the back of the eye socket to the top of the eye.
superior rectus.flow: Turns the eye upward (and slightly inward)

supinator.description: A deep muscle that wraps around the top of the radius from the outer elbow and the ulna.
supinator.flow: Turns the palm up, especially with the elbow straight

supraspinatus.description: A rotator cuff muscle filling the hollow above the spine of the shoulder blade; its tendon runs over the top of the shoulder joint.
supraspinatus.flow: Starts lifting the arm out to the side and holds the head of the arm bone in its socket

temporalis.description: A fan-shaped muscle over the side of the skull that narrows to a tendon on the jaw's coronoid process, under the cheekbone.
temporalis.flow: Closes the jaw; its back fibres pull the jaw backward

temporoparietalis.description: A thin, variable sheet of muscle above the ear, between frontalis and the ear muscles.
temporoparietalis.flow: Tightens the scalp and helps raise the ear slightly

tensor fasciae latae.description: A short muscle on the front outer hip that pulls on the iliotibial tract, the long band down the outside of the thigh.
tensor fasciae latae.flow: Helps flex and spread the hip and steadies the knee and pelvis when standing on one leg

tensor veli palatini.description: A thin muscle whose tendon hooks around a small bony pulley on the skull to fan out into the soft palate.
tensor veli palatini.flow: Tightens the soft palate and opens the auditory (ear) tube, as when yawning or swallowing

teres major.description: A thick, rounded muscle from the lower corner of the shoulder blade to the front of the upper arm bone, working like latissimus dorsi's little helper.
teres major.flow: Pulls the arm down and back and turns it inward

teres minor.description: A small rotator cuff muscle running along the outer edge of the shoulder blade, just below infraspinatus.
teres minor.flow: Turns the arm outward and steadies the shoulder joint

third lumbrical of foot.description: A small, worm-shaped muscle in the sole that runs from the long flexor tendons to the fourth toe.
third lumbrical of foot.flow: Bends the fourth toe at its base and straightens its other joints

third plantar interosseous of foot.description: A small muscle on the sole side between the foot bones, running to the little toe.
third plantar interosseous of foot.flow: Draws the little toe toward the second

thoracic rotator.description: Small, best-developed rotator muscles of the chest spine, each running from a side process to the vertebra above.
thoracic rotator.flow: Steady the chest vertebrae and help turn the spine

thyro-arytenoid.description: A broad muscle running alongside each vocal cord, from the thyroid cartilage back to the arytenoid cartilage.
thyro-arytenoid.flow: Relaxes and shortens the vocal cords, lowering pitch, and helps close the larynx

thyrohyoid.description: A short strap muscle continuing upward from the sternothyroid, from the thyroid cartilage to the hyoid bone.
thyrohyoid.flow: Pulls the hyoid bone down, or raises the voice box when the hyoid is held still

tibialis anterior.description: The muscle running down the front of the shin, just outside the shinbone, to the inner side of the foot.
tibialis anterior.flow: Lifts the foot up at the ankle (so the toes clear the ground) and turns its sole inward

tibialis posterior.description: The deepest muscle on the back of the leg; its tendon runs behind the inner ankle to the bones of the arch.
tibialis posterior.flow: Points the foot down, turns its sole inward and holds up the arch

transverse arytenoid.description: An unpaired muscle that runs straight across the back of the two arytenoid cartilages.
transverse arytenoid.flow: Draws the arytenoid cartilages together, closing the back of the gap between the vocal cords

transverse head of adductor hallucis.description: The small head of adductor hallucis that runs across the sole under the bases of the toes.
transverse head of adductor hallucis.flow: Draws the big toe toward the others and supports the front of the arch

transverse head of adductor pollicis.description: The lower, fan-shaped head of adductor pollicis, starting from the third hand bone, deep in the palm.
transverse head of adductor pollicis.flow: Pulls the thumb toward the palm, as in a key grip

transverse part of trapezius.description: The middle, horizontal fibres of the trapezius, running from the upper chest vertebrae across to the top of the shoulder blade.
transverse part of trapezius.flow: Pulls the shoulder blades back together

transversus abdominis.description: The deepest of the three flat abdominal muscles, its fibres running horizontally around the belly like a corset.
transversus abdominis.flow: Squeezes the belly and stiffens the trunk before you lift or move

transversus thoracis.description: A thin muscle on the inside of the front chest wall, fanning out from the lower breastbone to the rib cartilages.
transversus thoracis.flow: Pulls the rib cartilages down to help breathe out

ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris.description: The head of flexor carpi ulnaris that starts along the back edge of the ulna; the ulnar nerve passes between its two heads.
ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris.flow: Bends the wrist and tips the hand toward the little finger

ulnar head of pronator teres.description: The small, deep head of pronator teres, starting from the ulna and joining the humeral head.

uvular muscle.description: A small paired muscle running within the uvula, the fleshy tab hanging from the back of the soft palate.
uvular muscle.flow: Shortens and lifts the uvula to help close off the nasal cavity when swallowing

vastus intermedius.description: The quadriceps muscle lying deep under rectus femoris, directly on the front of the thigh bone.

vastus lateralis.description: The largest quadriceps muscle, forming the outside of the front of the thigh.

vastus medialis.description: The quadriceps muscle on the inner front thigh, forming the teardrop bulge above the knee.
vastus medialis.flow: Straightens the knee and keeps the kneecap tracking straight

vertical intermediate part of longus col.description: The central, vertical part of longus colli, lying directly on the front of the neck vertebrae.
vertical intermediate part of longus col.flow: Bends the neck forward and steadies it

vocalis.description: The innermost part of the thyro-arytenoid, lying within the vocal cord itself.
vocalis.flow: Fine-tunes the tension of the vocal cords for pitch and voice quality

zygomaticus major.description: The main smiling muscle, a strap running from the cheekbone down to the corner of the mouth.
zygomaticus major.flow: Pulls the corner of the mouth up and out into a smile

zygomaticus minor.description: A thin strap from the cheekbone to the upper lip, just inside zygomaticus major.
zygomaticus minor.flow: Raises the upper lip, showing the upper teeth
